plan: Given my value of $9, I aim to bid conservatively to maximize profit. I anticipate others may bid close to their values. If I bid too high, I risk overpaying. If I bid too low, I might miss out on winning. A bid slightly below my value, like $8, balances winning potential and minimizing loss. This strategy assumes others bid near their values and avoids overbidding.

Given my value of $40, I aim to bid high enough to win but not so high that I overpay. Assuming Andy and Charles have random values between $0 and $49, they might bid close to their values. To maximize profit, I will bid slightly above the expected average value, around $24.5, to ensure a good chance of winning without overpaying significantly.

Given my value of $32, I aim to maximize profit by bidding slightly below my value to ensure a positive payoff if I win. Assuming Andy and Betty bid close to their values, I anticipate bids around $25-$35. To outbid them without overpaying, I will bid $30. This balances the risk of losing with the potential profit, as winning with a bid of $30 against a second-highest bid of $28 would yield a $2 profit.
